As pointed out by Boris
column2: the defines for bits in IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL

column1: are quite a mouthful
column2: especially the VMX bits which must differentiate

column1: between enabling VMX inside and outside SMX (TXT) operation.  Rename the
MSR and its bit defines to abbreviate FEATURE_CONTROL as FEAT_CTL to
make them a little friendlier on the eyes.
Arguably
column2: the MSR itself should keep the full IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL name

column1: to match Intel's SDM
column2: but a future patch will add a dedicated Kconfig

column1: file and functions for the MSR. Using the full name for those assets is
rather unwieldy
column2: so bite the bullet and use IA32_FEAT_CTL so that its

column1: nomenclature is consistent throughout the kernel.
Opportunistically
column2: fix a few other annoyances with the defines:

column1: - Relocate the bit defines so that they immediately follow the MSR
define
column2: e.g. aren't mistaken as belonging to MISC_FEATURE_CONTROL.

column1: - Add whitespace around the block of feature control defines to make
it clear they're all related.
- Use BIT() instead of manually encoding the bit shift.
- Use ""VMX"" instead of ""VMXON"" to match the SDM.
- Append ""_ENABLED"" to the LMCE (Local Machine Check Exception) bit to
be consistent with the kernel's verbiage used for all other feature
control bits.  Note
column2: the SDM refers to the LMCE bit as LMCE_ON

column1: likely to differentiate it from IA32_MCG_EXT_CTL.LMCE_EN.  Ignore
the (literal) one-off usage of _ON
